title: API Documentation Endpoints
description: Contracts for the Swagger UI documentation routes and the browser-based login page.

endpoints.description: Serves a self-contained HTML page with the Google Identity Services 'Sign in with Google' button. Not behind any auth gate — accessible to unauthenticated users. On successful sign-in, the JS callback POSTs the Google ID token to POST /auth/google, then redirects the browser to /docs.

200.notes: Contains Google Identity Services <script> tag with data-client_id set from GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID env var.

endpoints.summary: Redirect to the Swagger UI index page
endpoints.auth: required — session cookie (browser) or Authorization: Bearer header (API client)

302-login.description: Redirects to /auth/login when Accept: text/html and no valid session cookie is present

401.description: Unauthenticated API client request (no Accept: text/html, no valid Bearer token or cookie)

endpoints.summary: OpenAPI 3.0 schema document for the entire API
endpoints.auth: required — Authorization: Bearer header or session cookie

endpoints.summary: OpenAPI 3.0 schema document in YAML format
endpoints.auth: required — Authorization: Bearer header or session cookie

browserAccess.description: Set by POST /auth/google after successful sign-in. Used for browser navigation to /docs. Cookie properties: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, path=/, maxAge=7 days (matching JWT TTL).

apiClientAccess.description: Session JWT obtained from POST /auth/google. Used for API client access and Swagger UI 'Try it out' requests via the Authorize dialog.

swaggerUiScheme.description: OpenAPI 3.0 security scheme pre-configured in @fastify/swagger. Swagger UI renders an Authorize button; the developer pastes their session JWT to enable Try-it-out calls to protected endpoints.

notes: The auth gate uses a preHandler hook (not onRequest) — request.identity is populated by authPlugin in preHandler; onRequest fires before that and identity would be null.
Browser GET requests to /docs/* without a valid session cookie receive a 302 redirect to /auth/login.
API client requests to /docs/* without a valid Bearer token or cookie receive 401.
All /docs/* static asset routes (CSS, JS, fonts) are protected — the scoped plugin's preHandler applies to all sub-paths.
The OpenAPI document at /docs/json is auto-generated from Fastify route schema definitions; it is always in sync with the live server.
PORT must be fixed at 3000 — http://localhost:3000 must be registered as an authorized JavaScript origin in Google Cloud Console.
GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID must be included in GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS so the server's verifyIdToken() accepts tokens issued to the web client.
No server-side state is introduced beyond the session cookie — the schema document is computed on each request from the in-memory route registry.
